title: The co-projection for the twist
statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion of
separated finite-type
$k$-schemes and let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$. Then, for
$m\in\mathbf Z$,

$$
Ri^!\bigl(K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}\Lambda_X(m)[2m]\bigr)
\;\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\;
Ri^!K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_Z}\Lambda_Z(m)[2m]
$$

via [lem-pur-coprojection] with the
Tate twist object
$L=\Lambda_X(m)[2m]$ (invertibility follows from
[det-def-sp-tate-twist-locally-free] and the shift calculation, and
its derived restriction to $Z$ is $\Lambda_Z(m)[2m]$ by
[det-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients-twists]).

proof.text: Work at the finite coefficient stage $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ prescribed by [def-pur-conventions]. This is a finite ring by [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]; moreover $|\ell|_E=\ell^{-1}<1$, so $\ell\in\mathfrak m_E=(\varpi_E)$ and $\ell^n A_{E,n}=0$. Since $X$ is a $k$-scheme and $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, $\ell$ is invertible on $X$. Put $T=\Lambda_X(m)$ and $T^{-1}=\Lambda_X(-m)$. By [det-def-sp-tate-twist-locally-free], twisting by $T$ and by $T^{-1}$ are inverse autoequivalences: use $d=m$ if $m\geq0$, and exchange the equivalence and its inverse at $d=-m$ if $m<0$. Evaluating their composite on $\Lambda_X$ gives $T\otimes^L T^{-1}\cong\Lambda_X$. Set $L=T[2m]$ and $L^{-1}=T^{-1}[-2m]$. Choose a K-flat representative $P\to T$ as in [def-weil-derived-tensor], and represent $T^{-1}$ by a complex $Q$. In [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], the summand $(P[2m])^p\otimes(Q[-2m])^q$ of total degree $r=p+q$ is $P^{p+2m}\otimes Q^{q-2m}$. The change $(p,q)\mapsto(p+2m,q-2m)$ preserves the total degree; the shift signs and the tensor differential signs agree because $2m$ is even. It therefore defines a chain isomorphism $P[2m]\otimes Q[-2m]\cong P\otimes Q$. To check that this computes derived tensor, for any acyclic complex $B$, reindex $(p,q)\mapsto(p+2m,q)$: the degree-$r$ term of $P[2m]\otimes B$ identifies with the degree-$(r+2m)$ term of $P\otimes B$, and the differentials agree by the evenness of $2m$. Thus $P[2m]\otimes B\cong(P\otimes B)[2m]$ is acyclic, so $P[2m]$ is K-flat. Consequently $L\otimes^L L^{-1}\cong T\otimes^L T^{-1}\cong\Lambda_X$, supplying exactly the inverse datum of [pur9-cs-def-invertible].

source.place: Proof, invertibility of L=Lambda_X(m)[2m], expanded using the total tensor differential

proof.text: Apply [det-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients-twists] with $f=i$ and $d=m$ to get $i^{-1}\Lambda_X(m)\cong\Lambda_Z(m)$ with the coefficient-module structure. The hypotheses hold: $X$ and $Z$ are $k$-schemes and $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, hence $\ell$ is invertible on both. At finite level the derived module pullback is termwise inverse image, as specified in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]; termwise inverse image of the shifted complex has the same terms and differentials as the shift of its inverse image. We therefore obtain $\rho:Li^*L\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_Z(m)[2m]$.

source.place: Proof, identification of the restriction of the Tate twist

proof.text: Use [lem-pur-coprojection] with $W=X$, the given $K$, and the invertible object $L$ of Step 1. Its closed-immersion hypothesis is precisely the hypothesis on $i$. It gives the canonical isomorphism $Ri^!(K\otimes^L L)\xrightarrow{\sim}Ri^!K\otimes^L Li^*L$. Compose it with $1_{Ri^!K}\otimes^L\rho$ from Step 2. A functor sends an isomorphism and its inverse to inverse maps, so the latter map is an isomorphism. Substituting $L=\Lambda_X(m)[2m]$ gives exactly the displayed assertion, with the stipulated co-projection map.
